title: AI-Powered Math Tutoring: Platform for Personalized and Adaptive Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem that many current AI tutoring systems, especially in mathematics, are too reactive: they tend to provide direct answers rather than supporting deep understanding, structured practice, and individualized learning. The authors ask how AI tutoring can move beyond simple response generation toward guided, tool-assisted, and personalized learning experiences.

To address this, the paper proposes a multi-agent AI tutoring platform built around large language models, Socratic tutoring, dual-memory personalization, GraphRAG-based textbook retrieval, and DAG-based course planning. The system is designed to support adaptive feedback, targeted practice generation, exam revision planning, and retrieval-grounded explanations, with the Tutor Agent orchestrating specialized components such as memory, retrieval, task creation, and course planning.

The paper is primarily a system/design contribution rather than a student intervention study. It evaluates prompting and model choices using the MathDial benchmark, showing that a tutor prompt emphasizing Socratic questioning and scaffolding performs better than a base prompt on success and telling metrics, and that o3-mini(high) performs well on math problem-solving tasks. The authors conclude that the architecture is promising for personalized STEM learning, but they explicitly note that real student evaluation is still needed before claims about learning effectiveness can be made.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a system description and benchmark-validation paper without a real-student evaluation, randomization, or causal design. The authors explicitly note the lack of empirical learning-environment validation, so it does not meet strong evidence criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports promising benchmark improvements in guided tutoring behavior and math task accuracy, but these are component-level results rather than learner outcomes. Because no student learning gains are measured, the real-world impact remains unclear despite the potentially useful system design.

interventions.use_case: multi-agent GPT-4o-based math tutoring with Socratic questioning, adaptive feedback, textbook-grounded retrieval, and personalized exercise/course generation
AI tutoring platform designed as an intelligent tutoring environment with adaptive support, student modeling, and guided learning workflows

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that a pedagogically informed Tutor Prompt improved guided tutoring behavior in simulated MathDial dialogues, with higher Success@K and lower Telling@K than a Base Prompt. This indicates better support for self-explanation, metacognitive engagement, and independent problem solving, although the paper does not provide numeric effect sizes for these benchmark outcomes.
finding.measure: MathDial benchmark dialogue metrics: Success@K and Telling@K

finding.finding_summary: On the MathDial problem set, the system evaluated several LLMs with SymPy access for mathematical problem-solving accuracy. o3-mini(high) and Claude 3.5 Sonnet achieved the highest accuracy at 90.00%, followed by Gemini 2.0 Flash at 88.67%, while GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini were lower at 78.67% and 77.33%, respectively.
finding.measure: Problem-solving accuracy on MathDial math problems

finding.finding_summary: The paper emphasizes that the platform automates personalized exercise generation and structured course planning, reducing the need for manual authoring of practice items and learning paths. However, this is a system-design claim supported by benchmarked component performance rather than a direct teacher-workload study, and no quantitative workload reduction effect is reported.
finding.measure: Automated exercise generation and course-planning capability; component benchmark performance
